relevance_reason: The abstract reports whole-exome sequencing in two women with recurrent hydatidiform moles. One had a homozygous KASH5 variant and recurrent GTN, and her sister with recurrent moles died of metastatic GTN. The other had a heterozygous FOXL2 variant. Only the abstract was available.

findings.statement: In a woman with recurrent hydatidiform moles (RHM), Saharan et al. (2026) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a very rare homozygous variant in KASH5, p.(Arg196His). They confirmed the variant by Sanger sequencing. The authors concluded that their findings further support an association of KASH5 variants with RHM.
quotes: Exome sequencing identified a heterozygous deleterious variant in FOXL2 p.(Gly187Asp), reported in patients with premature ovarian insufficiency (POI), and a very rare homozygous variant in KASH5 p.(Arg196His).
selected candidate variants were validated by Sanger sequencing
Our findings further support the association of variants in these genes with RHM

findings.statement: Saharan et al. (2026) reported a woman with recurrent hydatidiform moles and a homozygous KASH5 variant who had recurrent gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN). Her sister also had recurrent moles and died of metastatic GTN. The authors highlighted the potential for severe, life-threatening progression to metastatic GTN.
quotes: The patient harboring the KASH5 variant experienced recurrent GTNs, and her sister who also had recurrent moles died of metastatic GTN.
highlighting the potential for severe, life-threatening progression to metastatic GTN

phenotypes.text: metastatic gestational trophoblastic neoplasia causing death

findings.statement: In a second woman with recurrent hydatidiform moles, Saharan et al. (2026) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a heterozygous deleterious variant in FOXL2, p.(Gly187Asp). This variant had previously been reported in patients with premature ovarian insufficiency.
quotes: Exome sequencing identified a heterozygous deleterious variant in FOXL2 p.(Gly187Asp), reported in patients with premature ovarian insufficiency (POI)

findings.statement: Saharan et al. (2026) reviewed published rates of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) in patients with recurrent hydatidiform moles and compared them between different genetic causes. They noted limitations in the current data that should be considered when interpreting overall risk.
quotes: we reviewed the literature for GTN rates in patients with RHM and compared them between different genetic etiologies
Reviewing GTN incidence per patient summarizes current data and their limitations that need to be taken into consideration when interpreting overall risk.

relevance_reason: The authors used exome sequencing in patients with recurrent hydatidiform mole and found biallelic variants in meiosis I genes (FOXL2, MAJIN, KASH5, SYCP2, HFM1, MEIOB). The molar tissues were androgenetic. They also studied Hfm1-null and Majin-null mice as models.

findings.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) reported biallelic deleterious variants in 6 genes (FOXL2, MAJIN, KASH5, SYCP2, MEIOB, and HFM1) in patients with recurrent androgenetic hydatidiform moles. Five of these genes are essential for meiosis I, and deficiency of these genes leads to premature ovarian insufficiency.
quotes: We identified biallelic deleterious variants in 6 genes, FOXL2, MAJIN, KASH5, SYCP2, MEIOB, and HFM1, in patients with androgenetic HMs, including a familial case of 3 affected members.
Five of these genes are essential for meiosis I, and their deficiencies lead to premature ovarian insufficiency.

findings.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) described an Iranian proband (1802) with 2 hydatidiform moles. She was born to consanguineous parents (third-degree cousins), and her sister had had 3 hydatidiform moles. A maternal aunt had 1 hydatidiform mole at age 23, was then unable to conceive, and adopted a child. The CHM from the affected sister was confirmed morphologically, and STR genotyping showed it was androgenetic monospermic.
quotes: analysis of the exome of proband 1802 (Iranian), with a history of 2 HMs

The patient is from a familial case of RHM and has a sister who has had three HMs. Interestingly, the maternal aunt of the proband also experienced one HM at the age of 23, could not conceive, and then adopted a child.

Genotype analysis using multiplex and/or simplex short tandem repeat (STR) markers was performed on 6 CHMs (MAJIN, n = 2; HFM1, n = 1; FOXL2, n = 3) and demonstrated that all of them are androgenetic monospermic

findings.statement: In the Iranian proband 1802, Rezaei et al. (2024) used exome sequencing to identify a novel homozygous protein-truncating HFM1 variant, c.3124dupT (p.Tyr1042LeufsTer7; NM_001017975), located in a 25-Mb run of homozygosity on chromosome 1. The variant was also homozygous in her affected sister and heterozygous in both parents, who are third-degree cousins. The ACMG criteria classified the variant as pathogenic.
quotes: identified a novel homozygous protein-truncating variant, NM_001017975:c.3124dupT, p.(Tyr1042Leufs*7), located in an ROH of 25 Mb on chromosome 1

Analysis of additional DNA samples from this family identified the same variant in a homozygous state in the affected sister and in a heterozygous state in the 2 parents (who are third-degree cousins) and the maternal aunt, 1922.

findings.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) found that the affected maternal aunt in the HFM1 family carried the c.3124dupT variant in compound heterozygosity with a second novel HFM1 variant, c.1159-1G>A. The c.1159-1G>A variant is predicted to abolish the splice acceptor site of exon 8 (SpliceAI score 1, Pangolin score 0.9) and was classified as likely pathogenic.
quotes: WES on blood DNA of the maternal aunt identified a second novel LP variant by the ACMG in HFM1, c.1159-1G>A, in a heterozygous state
Altogether, these findings demonstrated that the maternal aunt of the proband is compound heterozygous for 2 pathogenic (P)/LP HFM1 variants.

findings.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) described an Italian patient (1824) born to parents who are second- or third-degree cousins. She had 2 hydatidiform moles followed by secondary infertility, and at age 25 her bilateral ovarian volumes were markedly reduced (1.1 and 2.5 cm3). Her 2 CHMs lacked p57 expression and were androgenetic monospermic. One of them retained a maternal allele at a chromosome 13 marker.
quotes: patient 1824 (Italian), with 2 HMs followed by secondary infertility and substantially reduced bilateral ovarian volumes (1.1 cm3 and 2.5 cm3 at the age of 25 years as compared with the normal volume, 6.1 cm3 in women under the age of 30 years)

Additionally, 1 molar tissue from the patient with a biallelic mutation in MAJIN had a maternal, non-paternal, allele at marker D13S317 from chromosome 13, indicating that this AnCHM tissue had retained 1 maternal chromosome

findings.statement: In the Italian patient 1824, Rezaei et al. (2024) identified a novel homozygous MAJIN splice donor variant in exon 6, c.349+1G>T (NM_001037225.3), located in a 48.3-Mb run of homozygosity. The variant segregated from both consanguineous parents and was classified as likely pathogenic.
quotes: revealed a novel variant affecting the splice donor of exon 6, NM_001037225.3:c.349+1G>T, in a homozygous state and located in an ROH of 48.3 Mb
This variant is predicted to be likely pathogenic (LP) by the ACMG. The variant segregated from both parents, who are second- or third-degree cousins.

findings.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) found that the mother of patient 1824, a heterozygous carrier of the MAJIN likely pathogenic variant, had 1 molar pregnancy at age 21 and had always had irregular menses. Her molar tissue was p57-positive and had a triploid dispermic genome, consistent with a partial hydatidiform mole. The authors suggested that monoallelic variants in MAJIN, and perhaps in other meiotic genes, may underlie milder phenotypes.
quotes: Immunohistochemistry demonstrated positive p57 expression in the cytotrophoblast and stromal cells, which is in favor of the diagnosis of a PHM. Multiplex and simplex STR genotyping demonstrated a triploid dispermic genome
Interestingly, the patient’s mother reported that she had a molar pregnancy at age 21 and that her menses had always been irregular.
Altogether, these data suggested that carriers of monoallelic P/LP variants in MAJIN, and perhaps also in other meiotic genes, may underlie the milder phenotype of the remaining 70 negative patients.

findings.statement: In patient 1690, of South Asian ancestry, Rezaei et al. (2024) identified a novel homozygous FOXL2 missense variant, c.500T>C (p.Phe167Ser; NM_023067), in a 10.5-Mb run of homozygosity. She had 5 CHMs, 3 miscarriages, 1 stillbirth, and 1 live birth. The variant was classified as a variant of uncertain significance. The authors stated that this single variant did not allow conclusions about a causal role for FOXL2. Three of her CHMs were androgenetic monospermic.
quotes: analysis of the exome of patient 1690 (South Asian), with 5 CHMs, 3 MCs, 1 stillbirth, and 1 live birth, identified a novel missense variant, NM_023067:c.500T>C, p.(Phe167Ser), in a homozygous state located in a run of homozygosity (ROH) of 10.5 Mb
Since the identified missense is classified as VUS, this single variant does not allow conclusions regarding the causal role of FOXL2 in RHM

findings.statement: In a Jordanian patient (439) with 3 hydatidiform moles and 2 miscarriages, Rezaei et al. (2024) identified 2 KASH5 variants, c.1555C>T (p.Arg519Ter) and c.1604T>A (p.Leu535Gln; NM_144688). Only p.Arg519Ter was inherited from her mother, so the 2 variants were most likely on different parental chromosomes. L535Q had previously been reported in the homozygous state in 2 infertile Qatari brothers with azoospermia.
quotes: analysis of the exome of patient 439 (Jordanian), with 3 HMs and 2 MCs, identified 2 variants, NM_144688:c.1555C>T, p.(Arg519*), and c.1604T>A, p.(Leu535Gln), in a heterozygous state

Sanger sequencing validated the 2 variants in the proband and showed that only one of them, p.R519*, was inherited from her mother, and therefore, the 2 variants are most likely on 2 different parental chromosomes.

findings.statement: In an Egyptian patient (1954), born to second-degree cousins, Rezaei et al. (2024) identified a homozygous SYCP2 canonical splice acceptor variant in exon 27, c.2530-2A>G (NM_014258.4), in a 19.7-Mb run of homozygosity on chromosome 20. She had 4 CHMs and primary and secondary infertility. The variant was classified as pathogenic. One of her CHMs was confirmed morphologically and lacked p57 expression.
quotes: analysis of the exome of patient 1954 (Egyptian), with 4 CHMs and 2 years of primary and secondary infertility (before the first and after the third HM), identified a variant affecting the canonical acceptor splice site of exon 27, NM_014258.4:c.2530-2A>G, in a homozygous state
found in an ROH of 19.7 Mb on chromosome 20, which is in agreement with the known consanguinity between the patient’s parents (second-degree cousins)

findings.statement: In an Egyptian patient (2136), whose parents had first-degree consanguinity, Rezaei et al. (2024) identified a homozygous MEIOB nonsense variant, c.814C>T (p.Arg272Ter; NM_001163560.3), in a 3.5-Mb run of homozygosity on chromosome 16. She had 6 early miscarriages, 3 failed ICSI cycles, 1 hydatidiform mole, and low anti-Mullerian hormone. The variant had previously been reported in a Chinese patient with primary infertility and premature ovarian insufficiency.
quotes: it identified a recessive homozygous nonsense variant, NM_001163560.3:c.814C>T, p.(Arg272*), in an additional meiotic gene, MEIOB (meiosis specific with OB-fold), in proband 2136 (Egyptian), with a history of 6 early MCs, 3 failed intracytoplasmic sperm injection cycles, 1 HM, and low anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH)

findings.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) compared 15 patients with androgenetic recurrent hydatidiform mole and biallelic pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in 9 genes with 70 patients who were negative for such variants. The patients with biallelic variants had a more severe phenotype: they had only 1 live birth and 62 pregnancy losses, compared with 39 live births and 198 pregnancy losses in the negative group (P = 0.0007).
quotes: The 15 patients with biallelic P/LP variants had only 1 live birth (in the patient with a missense variant in FOXL2) and a total of 62 pregnancy losses (HM and MC), while the 70 patients with unexplained genetic etiology had a total of 39 live births and 198 pregnancy losses (2-tailed Fisher’s exact P value = 0.0007)

findings.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) screened 310 patients with reproductive loss for monoallelic loss-of-function variants in 494 ovarian and meiosis genes. They found 77 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in 55 genes in 68 patients (21.8%). BRCA2 and ZP3 variants were significantly enriched compared with gnomAD, and genes in the DNA metabolism protein class were enriched (P = 0.003). The authors concluded that such monoallelic variants most likely confer genetic susceptibility.
quotes: This analysis led to the identification of 77 different P/LP variants in 55 genes in 68 patients (21.8%)

Altogether, these data indicated that monoallelic P/LP variants in genes with roles in early stages of meiosis I are enriched in patients who have milder phenotypes and most likely confer on these patients a genetic susceptibility for RHM, recurrent MCs, and infertility.

findings.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) found that Hfm1-null fetal oocytes had impaired meiotic synapsis. At 17.5 dpc only 18% reached pachytene, most retained gamma-H2AX clouds, and MLH1 crossover foci were absent. At 4 dpp, very few oocytes remained in both Hfm1-null and Majin-null ovaries. Hfm1-null ovaries at 21 to 25 dpp were small but occasionally contained follicles.
quotes: By contrast, in Hfm1–/– ovaries at 17.5 dpc, only 18% of oocytes reached the pachytene stage and all the others were still at the zygotene stage (P < 0.001 by χ2 test).
Where chromosomes were synapsed, MLH1 foci, which mark crossover sites, were absent in Hfm1–/– oocytes
By contrast, in Majin–/– and Hfm1–/– ovaries, very few oocytes remained, while FOXL2-positive granulosa cells were scattered.

findings.statement: In in vitro maturation experiments, Rezaei et al. (2024) observed that oocytes from Hfm1-null mice progressed through meiosis, but their spindles were often positioned parallel to the ooplasmic membrane. Of the MII oocytes, 4 of 29 (14%) extruded all their chromosomes into the polar bodies. The authors noted that this resembles Mei1-null oocytes and proposed it as a mechanism for the formation of androgenetic complete moles.
quotes: A total of 4 out of 29 (14%) MII oocytes from Hfm1–/– females extruded all their chromosomes into polar bodies.
chromosomes were often seen scattered over the spindles, which were positioned parallel to the ooplasmic membranes
The occurrence of a common mechanism in two mouse models argues in favor of its plausibility at the origin of androgenetic HM formation in humans.

findings.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) suggested that meiosis I defects affecting synapsis and recombination have a major role in the genesis of androgenetic complete moles. They also suggested that recurrent androgenetic complete moles may be a sign of accelerated ovarian aging or a mild form of premature ovarian insufficiency, which would explain the increase in risk with advanced maternal age.
quotes: suggested a major role of defects in meiotic synapsis and recombination in the formation of AnCHM
The data from our study suggest that recurrent AnCHM may be a sign of accelerated ovarian aging or a milder form of POI before its manifestation by clinical and laboratory tests.
